transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Is there anything you'd like to ask me about?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, yes, I do have some questions. First, I'm wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening after my cataract surgery?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing some light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. That's considered light exercise, which is fine to do.

However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for about a month after surgery. So keep the gardening fairly gentle for now.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for the advice. I also wanted to know when I can start using my eye gel for dry eyes again.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question. It's safe to continue using your eye drops or gels for dry eyes after your surgery, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're running low on your eye gel, your GP should be able to provide more for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. I'm very sensitive to bright light at the moment. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you have significant pain when it's bright, or severe light sensitivity — especially if your eye is also red and painful — that's not normal, and we may need to assess that further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the explanation. One last question: should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

However, I don't have your specific details about how long ago your surgery was. If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay. 

When did you have your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I had my surgery about a week ago. It sounds like the blurriness might still be normal at this point, but I'll definitely reach out to my care team if it doesn't improve soon. Thank you for all your help, Dora—those are all the questions I had for today.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Just to confirm — have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you've answered all my questions. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and best of luck with your recovery!
